review_findings.output_leakage: none. solve(demonstrations, grid) reads only demos and the query input. verify() and the gate get queries=[{'input': grid}] and see no labels; tests compare labels only after both answers exist.
review_findings.hidden_parameter_inference: none. build_program ignores d4/palette; the emitted source is byte-identical across 30 d4/palette variants. Panel axis, frame, background and motion are read from pixels. Panel time order (+1/-1) is a hypothesis that every demo checks.
review_findings.ambiguous_fallbacks: none. There is no default, majority vote, intersection, demo skipping or reset. Zero survivors raises Inconsistent; disagreeing or inapplicable survivors raise Ambiguous.
review_findings.domain_narrowing: none. Fresh draws are the unmodified native sampler: 117/1000 frame-coloured motifs (the hard case), 522 upward motions, 386 one-row motifs, both widths and both frame counts. All 8 D4 transforms are used, including transposed and order-reversed views.
review_findings.hard_cases: Frame-coloured motifs (fg==frame) are solved correctly under the native rule. The archived reference solver's '+1 if motif colour == frame' rule is wrong on 493/493 such native samples (seeds 10000..13999).
review_findings.identifiability: Native family (extra=0): a single demo fixes ORDER in 6000/6000 single-demo checks, and 0 queries lacked evidence with 3 demos, so no demo resampling was needed. With zero demos the query is a context shortfall: the program and gate raise Ambiguous, and in 792/2000 both orders were applicable. Only one native output exists per input, so there is no intrinsic ambiguity.
review_findings.fixture_conflict: Canonical train pair 2 is built with validate(extra=1). random.seed(15323); generate() gives a byte-identical input whose native label has the motif at rows 11-12; canonical has rows 12-13. verify() uses each train pair as a query with all train pairs as demos. So no deterministic function of the input fits both the canonical and native labels, and a strict demo-consistent hypothesis set (native or global residual {-1,0,1}) has no survivor on all 16 variants. Feature-keyed residual rules are not identifiable: 'motif colour == frame' and 'step>=2 and moving down' both fit all 3 canonical demos but put the canonical test motif at rows 10-11 vs 11-12. Passing would require memorisation, outlier skipping or a fixture-fitted key that the native sampler refutes, so certification is refused.
